There's not a man wearing white gloves turning the pages of the latest Jackie Collins.

Put so much work into it. I mean, he.

He's done drawings, he's done extra thoughts and ideas, and it's very odd to think that that has probably gone now into the British Library, which I think is obligated to take a copy of every book published.

I mean, let's be honest, it's not gonna really. It's not gonna be on anyone's bookshelf. It'll be on their lavatory cistern, possibly next to their bed. But nevertheless, you know, it's hard back and it's got pages. It's a real book.

Yeah but if it had gone to charity, Rick, I'd have felt a little bit superior, a little bit smug. That would have kept me going for another six months. Whereas now it's just gone to a couple of oiks off the street, you know, who are…

f: "I thought it meant sort of on the nose, on the noooose." Ricky liked it: "Oh that's good, yeah."
ex: What gear have we got in here?
I never knew what that meant, O-N-O, I don't- I thought it meant sort of on the nose, on the noooose.
Oh that's good, yeah. Um- what have we got well tell 'em what we've got we've got to give away Steve.

q: Steve was devastated by a record-breaker buried ten feet underground who talked to people through a tube. What did the man manage while down there?
a: He began and ended a relationship with a woman
x: He got engaged to his pen pal
He wrote and sold a novel
He learned to play the trumpet
f: Single Steve said reading about "a man ten feet underground pulling women through a tube" made him ask himself "some very serious questions."
ex: What happened, right, he-he got in this box and, uh, he was buried, like, ten feet underground--
It was in a pub car park in Mansfield.

Yeah and the only way he could communicate, the only way he could only communicate was through this tube he had that went up to the surface and he could talk to people and I assume that was how he got oxygen. And, um, it said that while he…
Yeah, exactly, Rick. What I’m getting at is when you read that there’s a man ten feet underground pulling women through a tube--
You’ve got to sit yourself down and ask yourself some very serious questions.

q: Steve's schoolmate Mark Johnson, aged about ten, claimed he was in the Guinness Book of Records. What was his claim to fame?
a: He was in the crowd at a record-breaking baseball game
x: He'd eaten the most fish fingers in a minute
He was the youngest boy to swim the Channel
He had the longest school tie in Britain
f: Ricky: "I don't reckon Mark Johnson got his name on the list." Ross McWhirter would be going, "Well, that's the whole book if we list them all!"
ex: Yeah. I, um… there was a kid, I remember, at our school, Mark Johnson, when we were, like, ten, or something and we were talking about "Guinness Book of Records". Mark Johnson went, “Yeah, I’m in the ‘Guinness Book of Records.’”
I thought, “I’m intrigued. You’re a ten year old.”

I said, “Go on.” He went- now I don’t- does this qualify? Does this qualify? He claimed that he was in America once and he went to see, um, a baseball game and the- supposedly that game was the world record for the number of people in an…
I-I’ll tell you where it was the count--
And he claims he was there.
I don't reckon it was listed.

q: After Karl explained his Rockbusters answers, Ricky declared it the end of Rockbusters. What did Steve say he'd love to hear instead?
f: Ricky had been moaning about too many ads, but agreed: "So would I! That is, adverts are better than that."
ex: I can’t believe we even brought it back, Rick.
Right. I’m, I’m serious, that’s the end of Rockbusters.
Can I be honest with you?
I’d love to hear some adverts now instead of that.
So would I! That is, adverts are better than that.

q: Steve said every time Karl opens his mouth, it's the equivalent of what?
a: Crossing a rickety bridge in Indiana Jones
x: Defusing a bomb in a Bond film
f: Steve had noticed Karl's phone message to Ricky falling apart halfway through: "You might not make it to the other side."
ex: Shut up. Um, it struck me when we were listening to his phone call to you, at the very beginning of the show, I don’t know if- you might’ve missed that, but basically there was a message that Karl left for Ricky. But about halfway through…
That might, you might not make it to the other side.
I know! Yeah! Oh, look at him.

q: When Ricky finally invited Steve to a future birthday, what did Steve ask?
a: Do I need to wear the waiter's outfit again?
x: Will Jonathan be bringing a cat?
Is there room in the villa?
Do I need to bring my own drink?
f: Ricky had said that next year they'd have known each other "seven, eight years".
ex: Listen, Steve, me and you are gonna stay in touch whatever.
So, I mean, not- and not, probably not my birthday this year, but next year, we'd have known each other what, seven, eight years?
Er, well come, I tell you wha-

q: Steve pointed out that the slaves who built the pyramids couldn't just quit. Where did he joke they couldn't say they'd 'get a better gig'?
f: Steve: "It wasn't like, they can go: 'Well, I can get a better gig on the Sphinx!'"
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Society · 2009
ex: No, that's not... No. That wasn't the lack of choice given to most slaves.
The slaves who built the pyramids-- That wasn't an option for them. It wasn't like, they can go: "Well, I can get a better gig on the Sphinx!"

q: Mocking the 'treat others how you'd want to be treated' rule, what did Steve say he would want someone to do to him?
f: Ricky went first: he'd want someone to throw cake at him, "Because I'm a greedy bastard."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Society · 2009
ex: Also, this thing that every individual can go, "How would I want to be treated? Um, well, I'd want someone to throw cake at me."
I would want someone to steal my telly.

q: Ricky found a huge queue and just one cab outside in Manchester. What did Steve ask about the cab?
f: Ricky walked instead, in the wet and the rain. Steve: "Obviously, it's the North."
ex: It was, the - you know, it was nicer. I went outside and there was a ridiculous queue and sort of one cab.
And so, I walked. And it was okay, it was only down the road. A bit dark. It was wet and raining, of course.

q: Which Sunday-night programme does Steve say still gives him that 'Oh, I gotta go to school' feeling?
f: "I love it, but I'm just thinking, 'Oh, I gotta go to school.'" His fix: "I wish they put it on the weekend."
ex: I think it was because school was the next morning 'cause Antiques Roadshow still does that for me. I see the Antiques Roadshow, I love it, but I'm just thinking, "Oh, I gotta go to school." Or work tomorrow.
The Roadshow, I wish they put it on the weekend.

q: Steve said Ricky should be treated like the Bible and Shakespeare on Desert Island Discs. What did he mean?
a: He'd already be in Room 101 without anyone nominating him
x: He'd be the one book everyone takes with them
He'd be the only thing worth saving
f: Steve: "don't bother putting Ricky in Karl, he's already there." Ricky: "I'm already there, waiting, go on then."
ex: You know in Desert Island Discs, you always gets the complete works of Shakespeare and The Bible.
I think you should include Ricky Gervais, I think you should always be there already in Room 101, they don't have to nominate you, you always go in.
So, don't bother putting him in, don't bother putting Ricky in Karl, he's already there.
Yeah, he's, I'm already there, waiting, go on then.

q: After a holiday in shorts, Karl said his testicles felt "like they weren't me own". What did Steve suggest had happened?
a: He'd got them mixed up with someone else's on the flight back
x: He'd left his real ones on the beach
The hotel laundry had shrunk them
f: Steve: "You didn't get them mixed up, did you, on the way back? On the flight back? Someone else has got them."
ex: They just felt - well they felt like they weren't me own, d'you know what I mean? It - they sort of felt a bit like these are a --
There wasn't a bloke standing really close to you was there? And you just --
You didn't get them mixed up, did you, on the way back? On the flight back? Someone else has got them.

q: One of Karl's complaints about Steve involved a free XFM rucksack. What did Steve do?
a: Called it rubbish, then insisted he wanted it
x: Gave it to Ricky without asking
Used it as a bin for his sandwich wrappers
Swapped it for Karl's free T-shirt
f: Steve's defence: "Well it was free. I need it... I'll give that as a gift or something."
ex: You were like, "Ooh, what's this- what's this rubbish?"
Ricky said, "I'll have it! They're great!", you said, "No, I want it!"
Well it was free. I need it.
I'll give that as a gift or something.

q: Going through Karl's prize pile, why did Steve say you might want Stephen Poliakoff's The Lost Prince on DVD?
a: You'd never watch it, but it'd make you look slightly classy and arty
x: It's got a monkey in it
It's long enough to cure insomnia
It's the only DVD Karl has ever finished
f: "Probably never watch it, but it might look like you're slightly classy and arty." Ricky's only question: "Is there subtitles?"
ex: Rubbish. Uh, this is quite though, it's Paul Whitehouse's TV show Happiness, that's the first series on DVD.
We've also got Stephen Poliakoff's The Lost Prince. You can have that in your collection. Probably never watch it, but it might look like you're slightly classy and arty. And uh...

q: Steve said it was time for the Scottish Widow to move on from her late husband. How long did he say she'd been grieving?
f: Steve's message to her: "It's time to move on. He wouldn't want to see you like this."
ex: He worked hard on his lan--
"It's time to move on. He wouldn't want to see you like this--"

q: Imagining himself wooing the Scottish Widow, Steve announced he'd brought what for her to 'hop on the back' of?
f: Steve billed himself as "built like Oliver the chimpanzee", and Ricky added that they were "going off to the moors."
ex: Yeah. "He's built like a ch- he's built like Oliver the chimpanzee."
Yeah. "And he wants to get at it."

q: When they realised the call was still recording onto Karl's answerphone, what did Steve suggest they do?
a: Leave the rest of the show on it as a message
x: Read out all the Rockbusters answers
Let Claire practise her dialling on it
f: Steve's evil logic: "He's gotta listen to it all so he can delete it."
ex: Why don't we leave the rest of the show on his phone?
He's gotta listen to it all so he can delete it.

q: After Ricky passed on a Coleridge quote about Keats, Steve worried the show was getting a bit high brow. What did he ask Ricky for?
a: Any knob gags he could do, quickly
x: Another go at the gig guide
f: Steve: "I just think there's a lot of people who are going to be turning off."
ex: So er, the lead singer just called in, for that, he also, er, left a quote with me, er apparently, er errr, Coleridge said of Keats wasn't it, he’s er, like an arc angel slightly damaged,
Rick, i’m worried we’re getting a little bit high brow
Have we got any knob gags you could do? Quikly cos i just think there’s a lot of people who are going to be turning off

q: Ricky finally got Steve to admit how much his Gavin of West Hampstead haircut cost. What did he pay, tip included?
f: Steve called £22 "the princely sum" and joked he could have tipped with "one of those Habitat catalogues" instead.
ex: Ricky Gervais, for this haircut... I paid the princely sum- and I was proud of it. 22 notes.
But I went up to 24 because I was pleased with what I had. Little tip for him.
Two quid tip. I could have just given him one of those Habitat catalogues.

q: Steve got his parents' Volvo estate wedged across a narrow lane, with a stolen pig in the back. What rescue did he picture being needed?
a: A helicopter lowering a magnet to lift the car round
x: The fire brigade with a big crane
A farmer dragging it out with a tractor
The AA with a tow truck
f: Steve: "they're gonna have to send a helicopter to lower a magnet, onto the top of the car". Ricky: "You used to read a lot of comics didn't ya?"
ex: So they’re having a wild time, hilarious. So this time, now we get to a sort of dead end in the, in the road, and they say “well turn round, let’s go back to the party…” I’m thinking ‘fine’, try and do a three point turn in this very…
Was it loads of blokes with like pitchforks and flaming torches going “burn him; he’s playing with our pig…”

Exactly that, and, and so then, you know, I was so terrified that all I could think was there gonna have to send a helicopter to lower a magnet, onto the top of the car to lift the car up and put it the right way round.
You used to read a lot of comics didn’t ya?

q: Stuck in the lane with the pig, Steve asked "you know what I started doing?" What was it?
f: Worse still, the other guy the girl fancied "had to get into the driving seat and sort it out for me" while Steve wept gently in the back.
ex: So, you know what I started doing?
Just started crying, just slightly, started getting upset and the other guy that the girl fancied, he had to get into the driving seat and sort it out for me…

q: Steve said Karl's moon plot had no room for Suzanne. How did he imagine Karl leaving Earth when the world ends?
x: Leaving her a note on the fridge
Promising to send for her later
f: Steve: "There's no place for Suzanne. It'll just be you. 'I'm off, love.'" Karl reckoned Ricky would be ringing him asking, "can I come with ya?"
ex: And I've got somewhere to go and I know you’ll be calling me up saying, “Oh, can I come with ya?”
You’ve got, like, a few square foot, though.
You’re going to have stand deadly still--
On the moon, in your two square foot.
There’s no place for Suzanne. It’ll just be you. “I’m off, love.”

q: Karl's live clue described an insect sitting with its feet up having a fag while its mates grafted. What did Steve call it?
f: Steve had already chipped in about the hard-working ones: "Some of 'em haven't even got heads, they're still working."
ex: And all the other insects, all its mates an’ that are really, like, working. They’re grafting hard, they’re tidying up. Some of them are going out, getting the food.
Some of ‘em haven’t even got heads, they’re still working.

Some of them are, like, you know, rushing around, but it’s this one insect that’s just sat there with it’s feet up. And it’s, like, you know, just doing nothing and it’s annoying all the other ones, but its sat there--
But it’s sat there doing nothing, having a little, like, fag an’ that. What’s the song?

q: Steve compared how his parents deal with illness to how Karl's family does. What did he say Karl's dad would have done?
a: Popped down to the phone box to look for throat lozenges
x: Told him to walk it off down the chippy
Rubbed a bit of Vicks on the telly
Made him gargle with salt and vinegar
f: Steve's mum, on the other hand, phoned the doctor first thing: "They're snapping into action, they're trying to sort me out."
ex: I happened to be at my Mam and Dads, ma Mam and Dads, now I’m talking like you, when, when this, this sore throat really kicked in. So I thought I may as well stay and get a bit of the creature comforts of home.
Do you know what I pictured though when, when he told me?
See my parents aren’t like yours Karl. Your, your father would have popped down to the phone box and maybe looked to see if there was any kind of throat lozenges.
Yeah, whereas my Mum phones up the doctor first thing she can, I’m straight down there with my Dad. They’re snapping (snaps fingers) into action, they’re trying to sort me out.

q: Steve admitted his pub quiz plan was really a hostile takeover. Of Karl's three regular teammates, how many had he won over?
f: Steve: "One of which was his girlfriend. So I only had to work on him to try and get him to resign."
ex: So. It was a hostile take over and they- they, sort of, clubbed together.
To be honest with you, there's normally three regulars on his team - I got two of them on my side.
One of which was his girlfriend.
So, uhm, I only had to work on him to try and get him to resign--

q: Steve has photos of his late grandfather, in his sixties, on the beach. What was he wearing?
x: His pyjamas and a bowler hat
f: Steve: "Wearing a suit on the beach." He even suspected a knotted handkerchief, and reckoned "he wore a suit to bed."
ex: I’ve got photographs of one of my late grandfathers. He must have been in his sixties. On the beach wearing a suit.
Wearing a suit on the beach. I think he- I’ve got a feeling he’s even got a knotted handkerchief and a full three-piece flu- suit.
Cause I- my grandfather, in my mind, my grandfather was always wearing a suit.

q: During the sign-off, Steve suddenly shouted "Oi!" How did he explain it?
x: He'd spotted Ricky's cat in the studio
f: "I wasn't just a maniac," said Steve. Ricky: "Why is your knob out when you're shouting and waving at me?"
ex: (giggling) Sorry I just, I just want to explain why that. That's a greeting in. In. In Brazil--
Yeah, I wasn't. I wasn't just a maniac.
Why is your knob out when you're shouting and waving at me?

q: Steve's earliest memory, from when he was about 2, was sitting on a potty surrounded by what?
f: When Karl said he didn't remember that, Steve snapped: "No, you wouldn't remember now, would you, you weren't there."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The Human Body · 2010
ex: I remember, must have been about 2, sitting on a potty surrounded by Lego. I remember that very strong image I have of that.
No, you wouldn't remember now, would you, you weren't there.
What do you mean? You don't remember Steve sitting on a potty surrounded by Lego?
No, I mean I can't remember having a potty. I remember...
(shouting) I'm not suggesting you have the same memory!

q: At a cashpoint, a homeless woman asked for change. What awkward small talk did Steve's friend make with her?
a: The clocks going back meant an extra hour in bed
x: It was very mild for the time of year
Cashpoints charge you to take money out now
Christmas seems to start earlier every year
f: Steve was mortified on his friend's behalf: "I gave her two quid, I felt so bad."
ex: …so you got an extra hour in bed?

And uhm, I was at a cashpoint with a friend of mine, and there was a homeless person sat by the cashpoint, and ahm… we were getting some money out, she said, “Spare some change.” And my friend went, “Hhrr,” he was a bit awkward, he was…
I gave her two quid, I felt so bad.

q: Ricky voiced the attacking chimps' plan: "You go for the nose. I got his bollocks." What sort of chimps did Steve then picture?
a: New York gangster chimps, like the Sopranos
f: Steve first asked "What accent have they got there?" and then settled on: "Were they kind of New York gangster chimps? They're like Soprano chimps?"
ex: You go for the nose. I got his bollocks.
What accent have they got there?
Were they kind of New York gangster chimps? They're like Soprano chimps?

q: Steve admitted he felt self-conscious after buying an ironing board. Which shop did he buy it from?
f: He imagined people thinking: "He's 30, why hasn't he got an ironing board yet?"
ex: It's interesting because I bought an ironing board last week from Argos and I did feel a little bit self-conscious.
Because I thought, I thought people thinking, "He's 30, why hasn't he got an ironing board yet?"
No wonder he's a scruffy bastard.

q: Ricky said the chimpanzee was chosen for the typewriter theory because it can type. How did Steve explain the choice?
a: "They hadn't come across you at the time"
f: Steve: "It's because they hadn't come across you at the time." Ricky laughed and agreed the point was "to take out thought".
ex: It's like- it's like they're- they're used to show that there isn't consciousness. They- they- they chose the chimpanzee because it can type, presumably, at the keyboard--
It's because- it's because they hadn't come across you at the time.
(Laughing) Yeah. Yeah, it's to take out thought- out of it. It's to take out reason and trying, right--

q: Karl moaned that Ricky kept popping into his studio while he worked, asking if Ricky would do the same if Karl were a doctor. Steve's reply?
a: If Karl were a doctor, there'd be severe problems with the NHS
x: Karl would be struck off within a week
Ricky would be his only patient
f: Karl: "Three times this week I've been rushin' around, I walk past me little studio, he's sat in there."
ex: Three times this week I've been rushin' around, I walk past me little studio, he's sat in there, all right?
Now, because I've got this sort of job, I can get away with it. I said to him, "If I was a doctor--"
Would he keep coming to me practice?
If you were a doctor, there'd be severe problems with the NHS.

q: In Steve's story of the American man who woke from a long coma, what did he reply when asked how he felt?
f: Steve thought the reply "horny" was "quite witty for a man who'd been in a coma for many years."
ex: There's a guy in some small American town and he had a car crash, and he'd gone into a coma, and his wife had
Left him, she'd got on with her life because he'd been in a coma since then, and he had just woken up recently...
Ha, marriage wasn't working. He just wasn't paying her enough attention.

He actually had— she was pregnant the time so now his daughter is basically the same age as he was when he went into the coma. And he's just started coming around, he's just started making jokes, they said "how do you feel?", he said…

q: Ricky asked whether the listeners enjoyed the show as much as they did, and if not, did that make them bad people? What did Steve say it made them?
f: Steve "would imagine not" that the listeners enjoy it as much. Ricky agreed and added they were also "lucky, very lucky."
ex: No, I don't think so either...
But, does that... make us bad people?
No, I don't think it does...

q: Steve and a friend once listed words that should be rude but aren't, like 'cassock'. Which band did the friend always point out?
f: Ricky added "bollards" and suggested it could be another new feature: "We're featured up, aren't we?"
ex: Did I tell you before, my friend and I once listed words we thought should be rude but aren't, like cassock, and-
-and he always pointed out "The Blow Monkeys".
Yeah, it could be very rude, but isn't.
That could be a new feature couldn't it? We're featured up, aren't we?

q: Karl said polar bears are no use to us, just "sat on a block of ice, floating about". Where did Steve say Karl got his information?
f: Steve: "Once again, he got his information from Glacier Mint advert." Karl didn't back down, saying the struggle is "going to make them stronger."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Natural History · 2009
ex: Because if it's not nice, people go "Don't get another one in!" And they die out. The reason we've got loads of chickens and loads of 'cowses', is because we eat them. If we ate polar bears, we won't be short of them. Because you'd farm…
It's no use to us! It sounds harsh-
Once again, he got his information from Glacier Mint advert.

q: Reading out the 'typical Virgoan' from a zodiac book, which description made Steve shout "Look at Karl! Look at Karl!"?
a: "Cranium may seem too big in comparison with the face"
x: "Ears may stick out like jug handles"
"Arms may seem short for the body"
"Eyes may be set unusually far apart"
f: Steve went on: "Has an extremely large forehead! Has a high hairline." Ricky: "But how specific is that?"
ex: Okay? The physical appearance of the typical Virgoan?
Cranium may seem too big in comparison with the face. Look at Karl! Look at Karl!
Has an extremely large forehead! Has a high hairline.
That’s not true, though, is it?

q: Steve recalled an awards do where everyone wore tuxedos or suits and ties. What was Jono Coleman wearing?
a: Bermuda shorts and a Hawaiian shirt
x: A kilt and a bow tie
f: Steve wondered if Jono can actually wear trousers. Ricky predicted that at the next Sony's he'd come "in a grass skirt and a garland", limboing.
ex: Well yeah but we- (laughs) we went to one where everyone was in like, tuxedos or suits and ties...
...not Jono. Jono was wearing a pair of Bermuda shorts...
Big Bermuda shorts, knee length Bermuda shorts...

q: Hearing that Karl's mam kept him home in case he got blown into the road, Steve asked if that was why she got fired from where?
f: Steve pictured her ringing in to work: "I'm not coming in today, I might get blown into the road."
ex: Well me- me mam just said, uhh, "You might get blown into the road so don't go in."
She had so much faith in you, didn't she... as a human being?
Is that why she got fired from the pie shop?
"I'm not coming in today, I might get blown into the road."

q: Mocking Karl's birthday gloves for Suzanne, Steve asked whether they had his name sewn in them and what else?
a: A piece of string running over the back of his duffle coat
x: A matching bobble hat with a pom-pom
A price tag still on from Woolworths
A free mint tucked in each thumb
f: Steve was treating them as school-kid gloves on a string. Karl's defence was the same as always: "It's what she wanted."
ex: I've told ya before about buyin' presents, it's- it's--
Do those gloves have your name sewn in them?
And a piece of string... that ran over the back of your duffle coat?

q: The scavenger hunt list included "Take an unconventional animal for a walk in a park". What did Steve suggest an unconventional animal might be?
x: A cat that thinks it's a dog
A goldfish in a little pram
f: Ricky started it with "a dog that just doesn't play by the rules", then added one that "wees in a urinal. Standing up."
ex: (reading) "Take an unconventional animal for a walk in a park."
I think that can be a dog that just doesn’t play by the rules.
Yeah, that’s a dog that’s into Slipknot.
Yeah! That used to – that wees in a urinal. Standing up.

q: Steve watched Ricky explain the brain experiment to Karl. Which word did he say made Karl drift off and start pressing buttons on his phone?
f: Steve: "It was the word 'symbolism' that got him." Ricky's first words afterwards were: "When did I lose you?"
ex: Yeah, I know. You started off by explaining it and I remember you mentioned- I- cause I was watching the two of you as you were describing it to him. You said, “Of course, one side of the brain deals with, uh, symbolism.“ And as you said…
Pick up his mobile phone and start pressing buttons randomly.
And I'd-I thought, “It was the word ‘symbolism’ that got him” and I noticed- you took a moment longer and I think the first thing you said was, “When did I lose you?”
Yeah. I knew I’d lost him.

q: Steve couldn't see why rugby was still allowed in schools, given what had been removed from them in the 60s and 70s. What was it?
f: Steve: "I remember thinking, why are we allowed to still play this game?"
ex: I don't understand. What I remember is, I remember a teacher saying, you've got to play it very carefully because you can get seriously injured, you can hurt yourself, you can be crippled for life. I remember thinking, why are we allowed…
At school I was worried about cracking heads and a finger in the eye.
That worried me all the time, a finger in the eye.
But they removed the asbestos from schools in the 60s and 70s. But rugby is allowed to play. It's mental.

q: Steve's mum warned him he'd get bored of a Scalextric. She bought it anyway and he got bored straight away. What did he do then?
a: Pretended to love it and kept playing it, bored
x: Admitted she was right and sold it
Swapped it at school for a Walkman
Gave it to a cousin and asked for Lego
f: Playing it "monotonously, hating it", he told her: "I'm loving this, mum, this is absolutely brilliant, you were wrong, you were so wrong."
ex: "...you'll get bored of it and we'll have spent all that money and you'll be bored." And I was going, "No, I won't, I'll love it, I'll love it, I'll play with it forever." and they said, and she was going, "No, you won't, you won't." and I…
But I didn't tell her, I pretended I loved it, and so, like, I'd always be playing it monotonously, hating it...
...going, "I'm loving this, mum, this is absolutely brilliant, you were wrong, you were so wrong, I'm loving it."

q: Steve blamed Zoe Ball for poaching Karl. According to Steve, she can't find her own what to get on the show?
f: Steve: "She can't find her own, you know, gibbon to get on the show... don't start stealing ours."
ex: I blame Ball as well, to be honest.
I feel Ball is slightly responsible for it.
She can't find her own, you know, gibbon to get on the show.
She can't find her own, kind of, you know, loser, then... don't start stealing ours.

q: Ricky invited Fatboy Slim on the show, but Steve couldn't remember Fatboy Slim's real first name. What did Steve guess?
f: Steve: "What's his name? Ernie or something?" Karl corrected him: "Norman." Ricky couldn't stop laughing at "Ernie".
ex: What's his name? Ernie or something?

q: Steve said that if he'd been at dinner with Bowie, he'd be chanting in his head: "Don't mention..." what?
f: Steve: "Don't even bring it up. Don't even say you like it cause you don't know what he feels about it." Ricky confirmed he hadn't mentioned it.
ex: You didn’t, you didn’t mention Tin Machine.
I didn’t mention Tin Machine, no.
Cause I’d just be there just thinking, “Don’t mention Tin Machine, don‘t mention Tin Machine.”
“Don’t even bring it up. Don’t even men- don‘t-don’t even say you like it cause you don‘t know what he feels about it.”

q: Steve claimed Ricky panics when a car horn goes off outside. How did Steve say he calms him down?
a: "We're on the eighth floor. And it's across town."
x: "It's only a car, not a spider."

You know what I mean and then he’ll hear it outside. “Err!” “What’s that!? Is it coming through the door? Is it--”
“No, it’s alright, Rick. We’re on the eighth floor.”
“And it’s across town. It’s fine, don’t worry.”

q: Ricky couldn't remember the name of a talk show host who's "not Jerry Springer". Steve guessed Montel Williams, then which R&B singer?

q: Mocking the typing monkeys, Steve said they could at least have written a script for BJ and the Bear. What 'irony' did he point out about that show?
a: The bear was actually a monkey

There were two bears, both called BJ

ex: Yeah. At least a script for BJ And The Bear.
The irony being of course in BJ And The Bear that it was a monkey not a bear.

q: Steve's childhood disco got booked by everyone. What did a bunch of venture scouts do at one of his gigs?
a: Went mental and had a food fight

Why were you playing to venture scouts for?

Well, we got booked by everyone, Rick. We, we, we, I mean we started with weddings and local, you know, things. But we soon went up, I mean, at one point we played a massive gig, in a big tent in the middle of nowhere...
For some scouts and they absolutely loved us. Rage Against the Machine? Oh, they couldn't believe their luck.

q: As Ricky and Karl got nostalgic about shops being shut on Sundays, what did Steve sarcastically chip in with?
f: Karl had been remembering getting up early for bread before the shop shut. Ricky's reply to Steve: "Yeah. yeah, shut up."
ex: Uh, it's good because I remember I used to have to get up early to go and get some bread if we didn't have any in, because the shop would only be open for a couple of hours in the morning, whereas now -
Yeah, i remember that. i remember that. shops shut. and you couldn't get aspirin and stuff, certain things...
Exactly, nightmare on a sunday afternoon
Yeah that's right, yeah, pubs didn't open til 12 did they?
Oh, do you remember space hoppers?
Yeah. yeah, shut up. can i ask you something?

q: Why does Steve flick straight past interviews with Ricky when he's reading the paper on the Tube?
a: In case a bloke says, "Oh, reading about your mate, are you?"
x: Ricky always takes credit for his jokes
He can't face Ricky's photo before lunch
He gets jealous of Ricky's photo shoots

s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The World Cup · 2010
ex: If I'm on the tube and I'm flipping through the paper, sometimes there'll be an interview with you that I'm not aware is going to be in the paper and I have to flip on by because I don't want a bloke on the tube going, "Oh reading about…
"Don't get enough of him. Do you?" Do you know what i mean?

q: After Karl refused a kidney to the cheeky little kid, who did Steve reveal the kid went on to become?
f: Karl took the credit anyway: "Maybe I helped. It's like Darren Campbell all over again. I made him stronger."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The World Cup · 2010
ex: Hey, wait. Do you know who that kid went on to become?
Right. Well, maybe I helped. It's like Darren Campbell all over again. I made him stronger. I was tough with him. He saw how tough the world is.

q: Why had Karl kicked Steve off the pub quiz team?
a: He was getting uppity and trying to take it over
x: He kept shouting out wrong answers
He refused to buy a round
He was caught looking things up
f: Steve came crawling back to Karl: "You're not going to kick me off, are ya?" Karl: "Well, yeah." He was let back in.
ex: Talking of competitions, I remember last week there had been an argument that, um, Karl kicked Steve off the team because he was getting a little bit uppity and trying to take it over.
Pub quiz, yeah, but then, uh, you let him back in, didn’t ya?
Well, he was alright. He came to me afterwards and said, you know, “You’re not going to kick me off, are ya?”

q: After Karl left for Cornwall, Ricky predicted the locals would make him King. Steve compared it to the Ewoks in Return of the Jedi elevating which character because he could speak their language?
f: Ricky reckoned "the mayor is probably an animal" and "the townsfolk think like Karl", so Karl would "stay there and be made King".
ex: Because I think one, the mayor is probably an animal. --
And I imagine the townsfolk think like Karl.
Do you know what I mean? I imagine he’ll probably, he’ll stay there and be made King
Have you ever seen Return of the Jedi?
In Return of the Jedi, the Ewoks, the little furry creaturs, they see C3PEO and because he can talk and he can speak the language they actually elevate him--

q: What did a woman do at Piccadilly Circus Tube station that left Steve "livid"?
a: Stepped over the gap and said "Oh, that's dangerous!"
x: Stood still at the top of the escalator
Read the tannoy announcement out loud
Asked him which way Piccadilly Circus was
f: This despite a big sign and the tannoy both saying "mind the gap". Steve: "I wanted to slap her. There's always one in there, every day."
ex: Can I just nominate a woman that annoyed me today?

On the Tube. I got off at Piccadilly Circus. The sign says "Mind the gap!" Big sign saying "mind the gap", voice on the tannoy says "mind the gap"... Woman steps over the gap, goes "oh, that's dangerous!"
I was livid! I was annoyed. I wanted to slap her. There's always one in there, every day. As you walk down the street, I just feel like I want to squat certain people out the way.

q: Steve suspected Kirsty's Home Videos used canned laughter. Which cartoon did he say people forget had a studio audience?
f: Steve loved the idea of people "being shipped in" just "to watch a cartoon".
ex: A lot of people forget that "The Flintstones" had an audience.
If you re-watch "The Flintstones" there's laughter when Fred does something funny.
(Chuckling) The idea of people shipping- being shipped in--

q: Since everything annoys Ricky, where had Steve said Ricky should be locked up?
a: In a tower, like princesses in fairytales
x: In a lighthouse off the Cornish coast
In the stocks on a village green
In a monastery with a vow of silence
f: Ricky said he's not grumpy like Karl, he's "just annoyed". On the way in it was a man behind him, scuffing and clicking in Scholls.
ex: Yeah, I know you're happy with Suzanne and everything but apart from that, you're never happy. You are the most grumpy, moany thing in the world. I mean, I get annoyed but I'm always happy. I was annoyed here, I was happy coming here but…

...I'm just annoyed. You are just like "Uhh, the worlds on me. It's rubbish, this." I know the world's great, it's just sometimes people annoy me by being there. You know, but uhh... Steve said I should be locked in one of those towers…
In fairytales. Because eveyrthing annoys me. Umm. But you are... You're grumpy.

q: Steve doubted Karl could talk and press the buttons at the same time. What did he suggest buying from Argos?
f: Ricky added that Karl also struggles with "Walking and eating."
ex: I tell you this, I'm not trying to be disrespectful Karl but...I think maybe someone else should come in and press the buttons...'cause I'm not sure you're a cros- I don't think you can concentrate on talking and working at the same time.…
-yeah, I- for you it seems it's a bit like-
Aw no, don't say that look- he's gutted. No, there's a lot gone wrong here. I say- I say throw this desk out and get a real one. Seriously.
Well I think there's a Fisher-Price one you can buy in, uh, Argos that might be worth getting,

q: Steve said Ricky keeps turning up on lists of ideal dinner guests. What was Steve's first objection?
a: There'd be nothing left to go round for anyone else
x: He'd only talk about The Office
He'd laugh at his own jokes all night
He'd leave before the cheese board
f: Ricky didn't help his case: "And I'm always early." People think he'd be witty, Steve said, but "he'd just be stuffing his face for two hours."
ex: The number of times I've seen you on one of those. The ideal dinner guest.
Not the ideal dinner guest. Well, firstly, there'd be nothing else to go around for anyone else.
So by the time anyone. That'd be it. Yeah. Yeah. The ideal dinner is as long as he comes halfway through the meal.
And I think they mean, oh, it'd be funny because he'd be very witty and charming. No, he'd just be stuffing his face for two hours.

q: Steve was propositioned by a woman on a London street, which he said had never happened to him in London before. What did he say annoyed him about it?
a: He was on his mobile phone at the time
x: She asked him for directions first
f: Steve: "Who would like- what, am I going to hang up? 'Sorry mum, can I call you back?'"
ex: And what annoyed me about it. What- I wanted to pick her up on something was I was on my mobile phone.
It’s like, can you imagine, who would like- what, am I going to hang up? ‘Sorry mum, can I call you back? You know you say you want me to meet more women…’
‘And you know you sent me that 30 quid for my birthday?’
Exactly, yeah. ‘Sorry, Mr. Johnston. I’m really excited about the job. Can I call you back? I’m just going to negotiate with a whore.’

It was like- you could tell she was clearly probably desperate for crack or her latest fix of smack. So she was literally- the normal etiquette of prostitution, you know they hang around, they show some thigh. I’ve seen this in films.

q: Ricky said he'd once been mistaken for Johnny Vegas. How did Steve explain the mix-up?
a: Someone just thought he was a fat man with a beard

It was dark and Ricky was shouting

ex: W—I mean – I was mistaken for Johnny Vegas. Steve’s got a story about that, if you wanna, have a go at me –
Well, you, someone just thought you were a fat man with a beard, which is true.
Well don’t have a go at me ‘cause he said you looked –

q: Steve launched a feature to resurrect the career of an overlooked artist each week. Who did he start with?
f: Steve said Aimee Mann was Oscar-nominated for songs in Magnolia but put her album out herself over the internet, while Alanis was "shifting shedloads".
ex: Um, I want to resurrect the career of a different artist each week, this is an artist who's overlooked by the general public.
This is Aimee Mann, and, she always seems to get overlooked,
I think it’s called Red Vines. Play it, Karl.

You see, what upsets me is the way that, Aimee Mann, she’s written songs as good as that, it’s released as a single, she had to I think put the album from which that’s taken out by herself, over the internet, she was Oscar-nominated, for…

q: Steve wrote down the real name of the Bristol street he grew up on. What detail did Ricky say "worries me" most?
f: Ricky: "It's the apostrophe-S... Because that's blatant."
ex: That's— but listen, you know what worries me? It's the apostrophe-S.

q: Steve moaned that you never see boxers with glasses. Who did he name as his one bespectacled athletic role model?
f: Steve: "So I got no kind of athletic role models in that way, except Dennis Taylor." He added: "I could write a book on the difficulties of having glasses."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The English · 2009
ex: Exactly. This is the problem, isn't it? People don't think that you'd never see boxers with glasses.
Right, exactly. So I got no kind of athletic role models in that way, except Dennis Taylor.
(laughing) Oh god. A man with glasses. Me and my classes.
I'll tell you this. I could write a book on the difficulties of having glasses.

q: Claire suggested travel pillows for Steve's grandparents, who spend all their time in bed. What was Steve's objection?
a: They don't travel anywhere, except from vertical to almost horizontal
x: They'd just use them as tea cosies
They'd already been given twelve of them
f: Steve said he'd already used up bed socks and "ointment for bed blisters" as gift ideas, and his parents don't seem to have any hobbies.
ex: You know when you're travelling and- and your head sort of falls down like-

q: On the tube, some passengers spotted Steve sitting in front of his own poster and burst out laughing. What happened at the next station?
a: The same poster was there, so they got another passenger to laugh at him
x: He hid behind a copy of the Evening Standard
The poster had a moustache drawn on him
The passengers asked for his autograph
f: Ricky's 'translation' of what the first passenger said in German: "Das freaken goggleye", which he insisted means "elegant boy".
ex: But I'm still forced to, uh, I'm still forced to take the tube. And, uh, sat on the tube, and uh, it pulled up and outside the window, just happened to be on the station was one of the posters with us. So I was kind of there, not realising…
And these ba- these big, kind of, fat German or maybe Bavarian guys, uh, had got on...
Were they in lederhosen eating sausages?
Yeah, they were. And, uh, and I noticed

One of them kind of looked at me, then looked to the poster, then looked at me. Just just, happened to see it and wittered something to his friend in German, you know, I don't want to try and do an impression.

q: When The Guardian interviewed Ricky and Steve about their top ten albums, what did the paper call Steve all the way through?
f: Steve was gutted: "Stephen Mitchell. It's not even like Merchant!" Ricky had already introduced him at the top of the show as "Steve Mitchell".
ex: Did anyone read the Guardian yesterday? It was Steve's big ch—, we were interviewed together, Steve…
I've never been interviewed before in a paper, I've certainly never had my photo in a national paper before.

We were very excited, we loved the interview. It was talking about our top ten albums between us. We loved it, we talked really fast like... school kids, we were excited. It was a great interview and all the way through, it was, “Ricky…

q: While Steve dangled 30 feet up on a wire, what did the stunt crew swap the huge crash mats for?
a: Thin mats like teenage gymnasts use on Blue Peter
x: A paddling pool full of foam
f: "The really thin ones you used to use at school." The wire was the real safety net, which didn't reassure Steve one bit.
ex: So uhm… so they hoist me into the air on this thing, they do a couple of sort of uh, sort of demo versions, you know, gradually ease me up higher and higher so I can m—become acclimatized to it. And uhm they get, they get me about 30 feet…

And I’m looking down at this, I’m thinking now… they may as well have shouted up, “If you fall you’re done for, but we might be able to protect the equipment.” You know what I mean, it was so rubbish.

q: Karl said last week's show was 'a bit of a mess', so he'd sorted it out by keeping the same features. What was Steve's response?
a: He thought the features were the reason it was a mess
x: He said a mess is what the listeners tune in for
He blamed Ricky for not turning up sober
He suggested Karl take a week off instead
f: Steve: "I think that was the reason it was a mess to be honest." Karl insisted he'd "tightened it up" to keep people for longer.
ex: Right, over the next 2 hours then... last week was a bit of a mess...
... So I sorted it out. Same features, uhhhh...
I think that was the reason it was a mess to be honest.
You tightened it, you tightened it, you tightened the ship.
Tightened it up, tightened it up, and also, keeping people for longer.

q: Amid the confusion over Karl's Galileo Songs of Phrase, Steve said: "That sounds like a sort of B-side from..." which band?
f: Ricky was no wiser: "I do not know what that is! What is the phrase?!"
ex: I don't know what that is! karl! KARL! I do not know what that is! What is the phrase?!
I just was saying last week about everyone's raving about Galileo.
No! They're not! No. No. They're Not.
That sounds like a sort of B-side from The Buggles.

q: According to Ricky, how did Steve think Pharoahe Monch's name was pronounced?
f: Steve defended it: "Monch is a bit of a rubbish word, whereas 'Monk' brilliant."
ex: Pharoahe Monch, 'Got You', although Steve thinks it's Pharoahe 'Monk'.
It makes more sense, don't you think? Monch is a bit of a rubbish word, whereas 'Monk' brilliant.

q: Steve gave which song as an example of one ruined by being used on a Coke advert?
f: Steve sang "First time, first love" and said it was "ruined now cos that was on a Coke advert."
ex: But that's a song, any other songs ruined because of their association with things?
That song 'First Time' which was on the Coke ad (singing) “First time, first love”, ruined now cos that was on a Coke advert.
Was that, wasn't that Four Non Blondes
It was Robin Givens, wasn't it?

q: Steve admitted his new plasma TV was too big. How much did he say it cost?
f: Ricky guessed "three grand or somat" for the 42-inch screen; Steve corrected him upwards before calling the question "gauche".
ex: But I can't believe it, he talked about this— buying it, he's got a bit of cash now, of course. And what is it, 42 inches?
42-inch plasma screen. What'd it cost you, three grand or somat?
...three and a half, three and a half grand.
Three and a half grand, big spender. Of course it's too big.

q: After missing his flight home from the Edinburgh TV Festival, how much did Steve say he had to pay to upgrade to another ticket?
f: Steve made sure the figure was exact: "A hundred and sixty five quid. Let's get it right."
ex: Yeah, tha- that was- so that was just before I had to pay a hundred and sixty five pounds to upgrade to another ticket.
How did you not tell me that in the last hour?

A hundred and sixty five pounds, Ricky, I had to pay because we dropped you off at the train station. So I mean do you want to go halfs on that or what d’you wanna- how do you wanna deal with that- how d’you wanna sort that whole- that…

q: At the airport, why couldn't Steve pay for the new ticket with the first card he handed over?
f: Luckily Steve had another card. "Yeah I've got two cards." Ricky: "Oh that is depressing."
ex: Yeah but I handed over my initial card. She said, “A hundred sixty five quid there,” and I went, “Fine.” I handed over my card and, it was a Switch card, she went, “We don’t take Switch.”
I was thinking how- what am I gonna do then? I don’t know what I’m gonna do. I don’t know where I’m gonna get the money from.
What did you do in the end then? Cause did you have cash?
Well luckily I had another card.
And um, and she managed to accept that one but I- I don’t know what I would’ve done there. I don’t- genuinely don’t know what-
You didn’t tell me you had another card.

q: In the revived "Make Ricky Gervais Laugh" game, Steve said the bespectacled, stubbly rock star in the Sun photo looked like which puppet?
f: Steve: "He looks like he is a muppet... made of foam." He then declared the game's comeback "a roaring success."
ex: I'll tell you who he looks like, he looks like Zig I think from Zig and Zag.
He looks like he is a muppet….
Nice to see that game come back.

q: How did Steve describe Karl's face for the listeners at home?
a: Like a face drawn on a balloon that's been inflated about half full
x: Like a thumb with a smiley face drawn on it
Like a potato with two raisins pushed in
Like an egg balanced on a pillow
f: Steve: "It looks like a face you've drawn on a balloon. Very small, the rest of the head; huge."
ex: Can I tell you now, can I try and describe for people the face that Karl has. I’ll tell you what it’s like. It’s like if you draw, um, some eyes, a nose and a mouth on a balloon--
And then inflate it to about half full. That’s what Karl’s face looks like.
That’s what his head looks like. It looks like a face you’ve drawn on a balloon. Very small, the rest of the head; huge.

q: Steve pictured Karl ringing a newsreader to report insects falling from the sky. Which newsreader?
f: In Steve's version Karl begs, "Put it on the news, quick!" and then spots the bird: "Oh, there was a bird, sorry Trev!"
ex: I love the idea, he's straight on the phone to Trevor McDonald "Look, Trevor, there's this caterpillars, insects falling out the sky! They're pulling out the sky now! Put it on the news, quick!" "You sure that wasn't a bird?" "Oh, there…

q: Ricky enthused about the neat hole left when a maggot was pulled from a girl's neck on TV. What did Steve conclude?
a: Ricky had watched one show recommended by Karl and turned into Karl

The strong onions had gone to Ricky's head
Ricky had caught a parasite himself
f: "This is it, you watch one program recommended to you by Karl, you've turned into Karl." Steve: "You want a hole in your body?!"
ex: But why would you want to hold in your body like-
No It's got pulling something out, sort of like putting something out your body, It's sort of cleansing, isn't it?
I don't know what you're talking about
No, but it's sort of like, i dont know-
This is it, you watch one program recommended to you by Karl, you've turned into Karl.
You want a hole in your body?!

q: Steve cuts through Chinatown on his way to Xfm and insists it isn't a town at all. What is it, at best, according to Steve?
f: Ricky agreed: "Gerrard Street does not a town make." Steve: "You've had this little street for about a hundred years... It's not expanding."
ex: This is not... at best, what you’ve got here, is a novelty street.
Yeah. Gerrard Street does not a town make.
No! It’s not a town. You’ve had this little street for about a hundred years.
Just cos you’ve got a little pagoda.
You can’t just call it Chinatown, and claim it’s a town.

q: Steve recalled the Radio One Roadshow's Smiley Miley. According to Steve, what was Smiley Miley's actual job?
a: Organising the vans that carried the equipment
x: Reading the travel news between records
Handing out Radio One stickers to the crowd
Warming up the crowd before the DJs came on
f: "Smiley Miley was not a DJ lest we forget." Ricky's point to Karl: he got fame and money just "because he smiled a little bit".
ex: Smiley Miley's Mileage Game, if anyone remembers that, I mean- here's a man, right, who- who- whose job, Smiley Miley was not a DJ lest we forget, Smiley Miley was the guy that organised the vans...
To and from the roadshows. But 'cause he was such a crazy personality-
Because he smiled a little bit...

... he got recognition, Karl! Longevity, lots of money, and lives where he wants to live, the town that he wants to live in. Why don't you just enjoy the town that you've chosen to live in 'cause it's so good: London. Whe- what towns have…

q: Steve said all-you-can-eat buffets react to Rik Waller like a 1920s speakeasy. What does the front of the shop turn into?
f: Ricky imagined buffet owners shutting the door when they hear him coming, and Steve played the doorman: "Move on. On you go."
ex: I just imagine those people who run all you can eat buffets, when they hear him coming they shut the door.
It’s like one of those nineteen-twenty’s speakeasy. The front changes into a launderette.
“Just move on, Fats. It’s not--” “I can smell chip fat!” “No, no, no, no, no, no, no. Move on. On you go.”

q: What surprised Steve about Orville the duck?
a: He's still not potty trained, despite mastering speech
x: He's never once taken off his hat
He still hasn't learned to swim
He hasn't aged a day in years
f: "He's been wearing that nappy of his, for years! He can talk, he's mastered the power of speech!"
ex: Just a quick point about Orville - I'm surprised he's still not potty trained.
'Cause he's been, he’s been wearing that nappy of his, for years!
He can talk, he's mastered the power of speech!

q: Steve suggested Karl would get on TV more easily as the subject of what?
a: An Omnibus documentary called 'Living With Karl'
f: Steve's other idea was a Comic Relief appeal: "It won't all go to people abroad, you know. There's some people in this country who need our help."
ex: I think if you want to get on TV, Karl, you'd be better as the subject of, maybe, like, an Omnibus documentary.
Or maybe one of those, uhh, appeals in "Comic Relief"... "It won't all go to people abroad, you know. There's some people in this country who need our help."

q: Karl said the old woman downstairs is always sat reading a book every night. What did Steve suggest?
x: That she was spying on Karl
That she'd written the book herself
That she was reading Karl's Diary
f: "Are you sure she's not dead? ... The pages never turn, she never seems to finish it!" Then: "Her cats are dead around her!"
ex: Are you sure she's not dead?
Every time you look down there, she's just flicking through the- she's just reading this book! The pages never turn, she never seems to finish it!
She never moves from her chair!
Are you sur- are you sure the Chinese girl's goin-
Her cats are dead around her!

q: Teenage Steve sat alone for an hour and a half reading philosophy, hoping a girl would think him wise. When she finally walked in, what did she ask?
f: She was soon getting off with Martin Wells, who'd "been dancing around with no trousers on." Steve: "there's a valuable lesson learned."
ex: Um.. Must have sat there for about an hour and a half before anyone came in. And she came in eventually, and I thought, ding dong, this is it. She came in and said, "have you seen Martin Wells?"

I said, "I think you might be next door." She disappeared again. I gave her another 15 minutes on the hope that she'd come back. She didn't... went in the next room, she was getting off with Martin Wells.
Because he'd been dancing. He'd been dancing around with no trousers on.
So all I'll say is there's a valuable lesson learned.

q: While Steve was DJing to a thousand scouts in a marquee at a jamboree, which song did he put on that sent them wild?
f: Steve: "They were moshing, they were climbing up the poles. The organisers were going, 'Switch that off! Switch that off!'"
ex: Right, and I'll tell you this, we were playin' our stuff. They were lovin' it. They were dancing, it was in a big marquee, right?
I slapped on Smells Like Teen Spirit.

They went mad for it. They were moshing, they were climbing up the poles. The organisers were going, "Switch that off! Switch that off!" Right? They're going crazy, and I was there going, "No! That's what they like. I'm going to do it."…

q: Steve once went paintballing, but his glasses steamed up under the mask and he was shot straight away. How much did he say it cost him?
f: It began with Ricky saying Steve won't mosh at concerts "because he's scared his glasses might fall off". Steve: "It was pointless."
ex: He doesn't mosh at a concert because he's scared his glasses might fall off, of course he wouldn't go to the moon, they'd spin him around in training, his glasses would come off and that would be it, he'd feel sick.
My worry is that I'd have to cos, would I be able to wear them under the helmet?
Like, I went paintballing once and I had to wear the glasses underneath the mask and course it was hot weather it was awful it steamed up in there.
It was terrible, I couldn't see anything, I got shot straight away, I was out of the game. It was pointless. It cost me like eight quid.
